newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens car unit takes over airbag maker.
newsitem.headline: Siemens car unit takes over airbag maker.

text.p: Diversified German manufacturer Siemens AG said on Tuesday it would take over a maker of car safety systems by buying 60 percent of automotive supplier Magna MST Sicherheitstechnik GmbH.

The purchase, still subject to regulatory approval, raised Siemens's share of Magna unit PARS Passive Rueckhaltesysteme GmbH to 100 percent from 40 percent, Siemens Automotive Systems (AT) said. A price was not disclosed.

With PARS -- which supplies Audi AG, BMW AG, Ford Motor Co and Volkswagen AG -- Siemens has acquired one of Europe's most advanced crash-test facilities. PARS has 85 employees and posted sales of 22.3 million marks ($13.8 million) in the business year to September 30, 1996, up from 11.8 million the year before.
Siemens AT, with 15,000 employees, had 1995/96 sales of four billion marks, including 200 million in airbag electronics, and pretax profit of 111 million marks.
Magna is 80 percent owned by automotive systems and airbag supplier TRW Inc of the United States.
-- Neal Boudette, Bonn Newsroom, +49-228 26097150 ($ = 1.621 German Marks)
